A gun control nut vandalized the 9/11 Memorial Reflecting Pool with red spray paint in a broad daylight political stunt.

Jonathan Andrew Tijerina, 31, was arrested and charged with criminal mischief and making graffiti for tagging a section of the North Tower reflecting pool with the name of his website Monday evening, police said, according to CBS News New York.

“Juststopkillingkids.com,” read the red spray-painted markings written across the names of dozens of victims engraved into the memorial at the footprint of the Sept. 11, 2001 terror attack.

Tijerina, 31, took credit for the vile desecration, posting video of himself in the midst of the act.

The alleged vandal recorded the entire stunt from start to finish, capturing himself walking up to the memorial, pulling a spray can out of his bag and writing his message across several panels, according to several videos posted to Instagram.

Tijerina identified himself as the person behind the vandalism that cost over $2,500 in damages, according to police.

“My name is Jon Tijerina and I’ve just spray-painted ‘just stop killing kids’ on the 9/11 Memorial,” Tijerina boasted.

The 9/11 Memorial and Museums announced it had removed the spray paint, returning the memorial to its previous state.

“The 9/11 Memorial is a sacred place of reflection at the heart of a rebuilt World Trade Center that honors the 2,983 victims killed in the September 11, 2001 and February 26, 1993 terrorist attacks. Yesterday’s brief incident was swiftly addressed by security staff and law enforcement, and the impacted area was immediately restored to its commemorative state,” a spokesperson told CBS New York.

Tijerina’s website promoted “nonviolent civil resistance” as the answer to his campaign, saying it was the way to change laws and society.

Tijerina promoted his arrest as a win, attempting to get the attention of President Trump and NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani.

“On October 26, 2026, Jon Tijerina was arrested for spraying red paint on Freedom Tower in NYC. He is demanding that Trump and Mamdani enforce common-sense, highly popular demands with respect to guns such as Universal Background Checks and a National Gun Registry,” Tijerina’s organization wrote in a follow-up post.

He cited the mass shooting after the Florida A&M homecoming football game as a reason for his alleged vandalism.

Tijerina’s “civil resistance organization” made two demands to “Just Stop Killing Kids” – calling for universal background checks and universal gun registry.

“We have two specific, achievable demands. Both have majority public support. Both already exist in other high-income countries. Neither requires repealing the Second Amendment. We are not asking for the impossible — we are asking for what every other wealthy democracy already has,” the website states.

Tijerina complained Monday that another one of his political protests, a recent seven-day fast didn’t receive any attention.

His alleged weeklong protest was to demand 2 million affordable housing units be made available in the city within 5 years.
news.content: گزارش بیشتر ما را در نتایج جستجوی خود مشاهده کنید. مهره کنترل اسلحه استخر انعکاس یادبود 11 سپتامبر را با رنگ اسپری قرمز در یک شیرین کاری سیاسی در روز خراب کرد. جاناتان اندرو تیجرینا، 31 ساله، به دلیل برچسب زدن بخشی از برج شمالی که نام وب سایت New را با C گزارش می داد، دستگیر شد و به اتهام شرارت مجرمانه و ساخت گرافیتی متهم شد. یورک. com، علامت‌های قرمز رنگ شده با اسپری روی نام ده‌ها قربانی حک‌شده در بنای یادبود در ردپای حمله تروریستی 11 سپتامبر 2001 را می‌خواند. تیجرینا، 31 ساله، اعتبار این هتک حرمت را به عهده گرفت و ویدئویی از خود را در بحبوحه عمل منتشر کرد. طبق چندین ویدئوی منتشر شده در اینستاگرام، خرابکار مظنون کل شیرین کاری را از ابتدا تا انتها ضبط کرد، خود را در حال رفتن به سمت بنای یادبود، بیرون کشیدن یک اسپری از کیفش و نوشتن پیام خود در چندین پنل، بر اساس چندین ویدئوی منتشر شده در اینستاگرام ضبط کرد. به گفته پلیس، تیجرینا خود را به عنوان فردی پشت این خرابکاری معرفی کرد که بیش از 2500 دلار خسارت به بار آورد. تیجرینا به خود می بالید: «اسم من جان تیجرینا است و به تازگی روی یادبود 11 سپتامبر با اسپری نقاشی «فقط کشتن بچه ها را متوقف کن» نقاشی کردم. یادبود 11 سپتامبر و موزه ها اعلام کردند که رنگ اسپری را حذف کرده اند و بنای یادبود را به حالت قبلی خود باز می گرداند. 2983 قربانی در 11 سپتامبر 2001 و 26 فوریه 1993 کشته شدند.

Thomas Markle’s granddaughter said that the child-porn allegations against him are not a surprise because there was always “something off” with him.

“It doesn’t surprise me,” Meghan Markle’s niece Noelle Rasmussen told the Telegraph Tuesday, five days after it emerged that her 82-year-old grandfather was being investigated over a disturbing trove of porn.

“The more and more I think about it… it just doesn’t. I don’t know why it’s not a surprise,” said Rasmussen, whose mother, Samantha Markle, is the duchess’s half-sister.

“Maybe it was a vibe that I subconsciously got… something’s not right about a person, and you don’t actively register it. But your body tells you when something’s off,” she said of her few interactions with Markle.

Rasmussen stressed that she was never molested by her grandpa — but is tormented by the fear that others could have been.

“I’m glad that I had never been victimised or had the chance to be victimised,” she told the Telegraph from her home in New Mexico.

“I don’t think he would attack family, but when you do not know what somebody’s capable of, you can’t assume.”

For this reason, she said, she “100% backs” her aunt Meghan Markle’s decision to keep her young kids away from their now-accused granddad.

“I support her decision to prevent her kids from seeing him,” she said of Archie and Lilibet, Meghan’s kids with Prince Harry.

“I wouldn’t want my kids around somebody who was being accused of child molestation,” she said.

She was equally disturbed by allegations that a letter earlier warning about her grandpa was lost by UK cops — and never forwarded to the FBI to investigate Meghan’s US-based dad.

“It blows my mind,” Rasmussen said of the apparent police failure to handle the written in 2019 by Thomas Markle’s ex-wife, Roslyn Loveless.

“That is a failure on the police’s part…that is such a failure of the system. It’s embarrassing,” she said.

news.originalContent:
Vice president Takeshi Okada said responses to several World Cup controversies did not align with his personal values.

The vice president of Japan’s football association has quit, saying the “series of responses” to controversies surrounding the World Cup did not align with his personal values.

Takeshi Okada, who coached Japan at the World Cup in 1998 and again in 2010, stepped down a week after the head of Asian football said the region supported Gianni Infantino’s bid for re-election as FIFA president.

Asian Football Confederation (AFC) president Sheikh Salman bin Ibrahim al-Khalifa delivered the unequivocal backing at a meeting in Tokyo.

It came weeks after the AFC had joined football bodies in Europe and North America in condemning Infantino over his plan to open FIFA’s premium competitions such as the World Cup to private investors.

Infantino has faced calls to quit and lost the support of some associations in his bid to be re-elected to a fourth and final term.

Okada, who is one of three Japan Football Association (JFA) vice presidents, said he was stepping down “entirely of my own volition”.

“Throughout my career I have treasured the social value of sport based on my conviction that sport must be conducted with integrity,” he said.

“However, with regard to the series of responses surrounding the recent FIFA World Cup, there is a significant gap between those responses and my own beliefs, and as a sportsman I cannot accept them.”

Infantino, who apologised for the failed private investment project, has headed FIFA since 2016 and is running for re-election in March.

Two months ago the AFC and Sheikh Salman signalled they could turn on Infantino.

A joint letter with European body UEFA and CONCACAF, representing federations in North and Central America and the Caribbean, declared football “belongs to no individual”.

Okada said his decision had been “reached after careful and repeated deliberation”.

“Taking into account our relationship with the AFC and the impact on Japanese football, I do understand that there are practical reasons for aligning our stance with that of the AFC,” he said.
news.content:
تاکشی اوکادا، معاون رئیس‌جمهور گفت که واکنش‌ها به چندین جنجال جام جهانی با ارزش‌های شخصی او همخوانی ندارد. نایب رئیس اتحادیه فوتبال ژاپن از سمت خود کناره‌گیری کرد و گفت که «مجموعه پاسخ‌ها» به بحث‌های پیرامون جام جهانی با ارزش‌های شخصی او همخوانی ندارد. تاکشی اوکادا که در جام جهانی 1998 و بار دیگر در سال 2010 سرمربی ژاپن بود، یک هفته پس از اینکه رئیس فوتبال آسیا گفت که منطقه از پیشنهاد جیانی اینفانتینو برای انتخاب مجدد به عنوان رئیس فیفا حمایت می کند، از سمت خود کناره گیری کرد. این چند هفته پس از پیوستن کنفدراسیون فوتبال آسیا به نهادهای فوتبال در اروپا و آمریکای شمالی در محکوم کردن اینفانتینو به دلیل برنامه‌اش برای باز کردن رقابت‌های برتر فیفا مانند جام جهانی به روی سرمایه‌گذاران خصوصی رخ داد. اینفانتینو در تلاش برای انتخاب مجدد برای چهارمین و آخرین دوره با درخواست‌ها برای کناره‌گیری مواجه شده و حمایت برخی انجمن‌ها را از دست داده است. اوکادا، که یکی از سه نایب رئیس اتحادیه فوتبال ژاپن (JFA) است، گفت که "کاملاً به میل خودم" از سمت خود کناره گیری می کند. با این حال، با توجه به مجموعه ای از پاسخ ها در مورد جام جهانی اخیر، شکاف قابل توجهی بین این پاسخ ها و باورهای خودم وجود دارد و به عنوان یک ورزشکار نمی توانم آنها را بپذیرم.

Sitting at the base of a tree in Costa Rica, Dave L. cradled the trunk and wept.

After decades in the Army, Dave had learned to bury his emotions and push through pain — a habit reinforced by the rigid ideas about masculinity he grew up with.

Now, at the end of his fourth ayahuasca ceremony, the 44-year-old firefighter and former Ranger felt ready to let go of the emotional weight he had carried for years.

“I had trauma trapped in various places of my body, and I could  just feel it releasing,” Dave told The Post. “Like, for days, I feel like I was just releasing stuff that was holding me back in life.”

Dave had traveled to Costa Rica with 45 other American veterans and first responders to explore a controversial approach to healing the psychological and emotional wounds they carried home from war and emergency response.

There at Rythmia Life Advancement Center, the men spent a week immersed in ayahuasca ceremonies, counseling and meditation, confronting painful memories alongside others who understood the ghosts of their former lives.

The retreat, co-organized with Coming Home, a nonprofit dedicated to ending veteran suicide through access to psychedelic-assisted healing, coincided with the 25th anniversary of 9/11. The need for new approaches remains critical, as a 2026 Department of Veterans Affairs report recorded 6,488 veteran suicide deaths in 2024, at an average of 17.7 per day.

Once a hidden Amazonian secret, ayahuasca has sparked a major scientific movement for its potential to treat PTSD, depression and addiction. Yet the plant brew remains highly controversial, carrying steep physical and psychological risks that range from severe nausea to rare but dangerous psychiatric and medication complications.

For some seekers, the grueling journey pays off as clinical data increasingly links guided ayahuasca use to lasting relief, with participants reporting a profound spiritual lift and life-altering emotional growth.

Because its active psychedelic ingredient, DMT, remains illegal under federal law, thousands of Americans now travel to specialized wellness retreats abroad to experience the medicine under structured medical supervision at centers like Rythmia, where organizers combine the traditional practice with counseling and medical oversight.

“I wanted to gain the tools of how to be a balanced man in life,” said Dave about his interest in ayahuasca therapy. He admitted feeling as if his life was “falling apart without those tools.”

“I was taught a bunch of survival tools, but I wasn’t taught how to be gentle with myself, how to be emotionally available to those who are closest around me, which I feel like at this stage in the game — in my 40s — is like really important,” he added.

For seven days, Dave and his peers would have the space to slow down, reconnect with their emotions and explore a radically different kind of strength — one rooted in vulnerability, self-compassion and connection.

Nestled in Guanacaste, a sun-drenched coastal province, the retreat brought together Navy SEALs, Army Rangers, Green Berets, combat controllers, pararescuemen and other military personnel and first responders — men Dave described as “the toughest of tough men that you’ll ever run into in our culture.”

Each morning began with an hour of yoga, followed by individual and group counseling, educational classes and meditation and relaxation sessions, with stretches of unstructured time to visit the on-site mud spa or simply decompress.

After dark, the men gathered in tents with the center’s guides and staff to embark on a psychedelic healing journey. Each received a serving of the thick, bitter, dark-colored tea brewed from the ayahuasca plant’s leaves, the psychedelic effects of which could bring emotional revelations and sometimes dramatic reactions.

For Nate Brown, a Navy SEAL veteran and Coming Home’s founder, the opportunity to slow down marked a sharp departure from the pace that had defined these men’s careers.

“If you can imagine the way these gentlemen have been working their entire adult lives, everything’s about compression timelines under stress and everything,” he explained to The Post. “So to be able to take them somewhere and allow them to just unravel slowly over the course of a week and watch them rest in mind, body and spirit is just something beautiful to witness.”

He said the men looked “10 years younger” by the end of the retreat, referring to selfies participants took at the beginning and end of the week.

“They can’t feel anything but rage and anger, completely out of touch with, you know, the sweetness, the softness and the beauty that they all deserve,” Brown said. “And over the course of that week, watching that shift, watching the medicine start opening up these parts of their soul, is something beautiful and amazing.

“To watch these men come out of ceremony and to hug one another and to cry, you can’t put a price on that.”

Those embraces and tears offered a glimpse of the bond forming among the men. Dave said that watching other participants break down helped everyone access feelings they might ordinarily suppress. Rather than retreating from the motion, the men leaned in together.

“You’ve got a room full of killers, people who will run into burning buildings, people that run to gunfire instead of away from it,” he said. “And when you’re in that room, and one man weeps because he’s feeling lost or feeling grief, that is contagious.”

Photojournalist John Moore, a Pulitzer Prize winner known for documenting conflict in Afghanistan, Iraq and other war zones, witnessed the change while photographing the weeklong experience, including portions of the ceremonies — a first-time exception to the strict privacy rules that typically govern Rythmia.

“People think of special forces veterans as being hard characters, but everyone is human,” he told The Post. “I thought it was touching and really impressive that these former warriors were accessing their human side and trying to become better people, better spouses, better parents and better neighbors.”

Moore said he noticed participants growing more comfortable expressing emotions over the course of the week, with a shared “culture of respect” helping them feel safe enough to let their guard down.

Tears weren’t the only thing flowing during the ceremonies.

Ayahuasca can trigger a decidedly physical experience, from bouts of vomiting and diarrhea to sweating, yawning and repeated trips to the bathroom — reactions traditionally known as purging, which some interpret as a form of emotional or spiritual release.

Rythmia’s chief medical officer, Dr. Jeff McNairy, told The Post that roughly half of the participants vomited during a given night’s ceremony. Staff members were close at hand, promptly cleaning and returning buckets as needed.

“When people ask me, ‘What’s ayahuasca best for?’ my No. 1 answer is trauma,” McNairy, a psychiatrist, said.

During a traumatic event, he explained, fear, doubt and other feelings can interfere with survival. A soldier in combat, for instance, may need to push those emotions aside to act quickly under threat. When people cannot later process those experiences, the associated emotions can continue to affect their lives, sometimes contributing to anger, disassociation or substance abuse.

The purging is “a psychosomatic response” of the trauma being released, said McNairy.

While the journey is notoriously taxing — with about 70% of users experiencing acute nausea and more than half reporting unsettling psychological side effects like deep disconnection — severe medical risks also loom large. If combined with standard SSRI antidepressants, the brew can trigger fatal serotonin syndrome or even prolonged psychotic episodes in individuals with pre-existing psychiatric vulnerabilities.

Before the retreat, Rythmia and Coming Home screened the men’s medical histories, medications and mental health before confirming their stays.

The organizations also assisted the participants with a 30-day preparation period that recommends mostly vegetarian or vegan-style meals, fewer strongly spiced foods and reduced exposure to distressing news stories and horror movies.

“We have all these medical people and, you know, sort of Western stuff, but then we also have 45 shamans who work there, so it’s this cool blend of both indigenous and Western together,” said McNairy, noting the center’s 24-hour medical staff of five doctors, 12 registered nurses and additional paramedics available.

For Dave, the most meaningful changes emerged after he returned to everyday life, where the relationships, responsibilities and pressures that shaped his experience of trauma remained.

The first sign that something had shifted was a welcome absence.

“The war that I usually wage in between my own ear at any given moment is way quieter, way softer,” he said.

Dave doesn’t consider ayahuasca a universal solution, nor does he claim that one retreat can completely erase trauma. Still, the experience offered a new way to approach feelings he had spent years pushing aside and the chance to do that alongside men who understood the weight of what he carried.

“When you walk away from the ceremony back into life, you can just be met head on with those challenges, with that pain, those dark emotions, those things of daily life that we all push away,” he said.

“Now we face it with a new courage and without fear and realize that it doesn’t kill us and that it’s OK, that actually makes us feel more alive.”

Two of the Alexander brothers worked in luxury real estate — but were they the real deal?

On Tuesday, as three Alexander brothers — Tal and twins Oren and Alon — were sentenced in Manhattan Federal Court to 30 years each for the heinous and “monstrous” crimes of drugging and raping scores of women over a decade, The Post takes a look at their smoke-and-mirrors lifestyle.

The siblings were accused of using their luxury lifestyle as a way to lure unsuspecting women into their orbit.

Their lives in New York included renting trophy apartments, but never owning them.

One apartment was at 432 Park Ave., while the other was at 158 Mercer St. where Mark Madoff, the eldest son of the late Ponzi scammer Bernie Madoff, hanged himself in 2010.

And while Oren, 39, and Tal, 40 flew on private planes, they were there as rich people’s guests, allegedly “luring” high-net-worth men to coke- and sex-fueled parties as a way to recruit, and to keep, clients, several top brokers told The Post.

“That is just the tip of the iceberg,” said one broker who knows some women who attended the parties and helped recruit other women. “These guys were too young to make that much money. They were looking for entree to the upper echelons of high risk business relations — through the parties and the women.”

(The eldest brother, Niv Alexander, married to cruise heiress Cassie Arison, has not been accused of any crime and has stayed out of the spotlight, while a younger brother, Oren’s twin Alon — who worked in security and was married to Shani Zigron, who has not been accused of any crime — was also charged and convicted of sex-trafficking crimes.)

The home that Tal Alexander rented at 432 Park, which Oren once shared, was home to Tal’s estranged wife — who filed for divorce in January 2025, just weeks after the horrific allegations surfaced — and child until April 2025. Oren and Alon’s wives were not in court on Tuesday, nor were the brothers’ parents.

Outside of Manhattan, Oren, Tal and Alon still have a stake in a Florida home and, through a family-linked company, an Aspen ranch, records show.

The three bought a site at 3541 Flamingo Drive in Miami Beach in 2014 for around $3.42 million, developed a mansion there with their father, Shlomy, and sold it in 2023 for $27.5 million.

In 2020, Oren paid $10 million for 2135 Lake Ave. on the Sunset Islands, demolished the house and built a 10,000-square-foot mansion. He and his wife, Brazilian model Kamila Hansen, then sold it in June 2025 for $51.5 million.

Also in 2020, Tal paid $3.1 million for a half-acre lot at 2687 Flamingo Drive, where the family’s Alexander Group built a house. Tal sold it for $33 million to a land trust managed by Joseph Lebowicz, in a deal that closed in the summer of 2026, according to reports.

The brothers still hold 1611 W. 24th St. on the Sunset Islands through an LLC managed by Oren, which bought it in 2021 for $9.8 million. It was listed for rent at $55,000 a month in April 2025, and the family was still renting it out as of September 2026. City National Bank’s foreclosure suit on that house was dismissed with prejudice earlier this month.

A family-linked company also bought a 48-acre ranch outside Aspen in 2020 for $3.3 million.

The Alexander brothers’ real estate colleagues also called them difficult to deal with.

“As brokers, they were ruthless and found ways to kick other brokers off deals,” said one, explaining that they misrepresented their role in the record-breaking Ken Griffin deal at 220 Central Park South, because they portrayed themselves as having a relationship with the developer and the residences that they did not have.

“Tal tried to handle the deal but he was so incompetent that [Douglas Elliman CEO] Howard Lorber had to come in. Tal only got the deal because he led Ken Griffin to believe that he was the only who had access to the apartments” that Griffin wanted to buy, a source with knowledge of the deal told The Post on Tuesday.

After the sentencing, the source said: “It’s telling that not a single person in the real estate community stood up for them. They were despised.”

For now, it’s still difficult to know the full extent of their real estate holdings and what they will be able to keep, real estate lawyers say.

“If they sell anything, any money from any sale would have to go to repay any victims who are plaintiffs — and there are civil as well as criminal lawsuits. It will be interesting to find out if they did any asset protection,” said one lawyer familiar with asset hiding and protection.

“My feeling is that they probably moved quickly to protect their assets. But there is also at least one divorce, and that process is its own colonoscopy. It’s possible that they [stashed assets] offshore, but the likelihood of success is not very high. When your focus is staying out of jail, everything else is secondary and these guys at a certain point realized that their entire lives were collapsing around them.”

news.originalContent:
UK chancellor to present an autumn budget amid rising living costs and energy bills.

British Chancellor John Healey will set out the country’s autumn budget, the government’s tax and spending plans, the first under Prime Minister Andy Burnham’s premiership amid high inflation and government spending levels.

While the budget will be announced in parliament on Wednesday at 12.30 GMT, speculation about what it will lay out has ranged from a series of tax announcements to commitments to defence spending.

But the country continues to deal with a rising cost-of-living crisis and energy bills are expected to see their biggest rise in four years in January due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East.

As total United Kingdom borrowing broke through the 3 trillion pounds ($3.99 trillion) barrier for the first time in September, the country is already spending 100 billion pounds ($133bn) each year just on servicing that debt.

Despite that challenge, the chancellor has said the budget will move “money and power out of Westminster and into every postcode around Britain”.

In a speech last month, Healey said that he and Burnham were in “lockstep” in meeting fiscal rules, “to balancing the books, with a buffer to protect against uncertainty, to control borrowing to bear down on inflation, and reducing long-term pressures on our public finances”.

Gregory Thwaites, interim chief economist at the British think tank, Resolution Foundation, told Al Jazeera he is expecting a “relatively small budget given the limited room for maneuvre the government has”.

“A bit of action to offset high living costs,” but “most big decisions postponed to next year.”

Following the two budgets from former Chancellor Rachel Reeves, which included big tax and spending increases, Healey’s budget is expected to take a more “steady as she goes” line, which some say is the wrong approach.

Here’s how he will be expected to achieve that.

On Monday, Burnham said Healey would set out a plan to fully fund the government’s defence plans and commitments, telling ITV’s Good Morning Britain that his government’s first challenge was financing the already announced defence investment plan.

Announced in June, the plan is backed by 298 billion pounds ($396bn) of investment and will transform the armed forces as the country moves to “warfighting readiness” and stepping up “European security”, according to a government policy paper.

But Burnham said it was “crucial that we have a funded plan that we can then implement, and we will set out more details on Wednesday as to how we’ve done that”.

He added that NATO commitments of spending 3 percent of gross domestic product (GDP) on defence spending by 2030 and 3.5 percent by 2035 are included in the pathway, explaining that national security issues were “at the top of the priority list”.

As it stands, Britain spends about 2.6 percent of its GDP on defence.

The Guardian reported that on defence spending, Healey aims to close a 4.7-billion-pound ($6.2bn) funding gap in the government’s plan inherited from the previous Labour Party leader, with cuts to other departmental budgets likely to fund it.

Government borrowing and inflation continue to rise, which is a potential spanner in the works for proposed spending.

Last week, UK inflation and government borrowing both hit their highest levels in a year.

According to the Office for National Statistics, borrowing was nearly 25 billion pounds ($33bn) last month alone, “a little higher than a year earlier, as spending, including higher debt interest costs, increased more than government income, partly reflecting the impacts of inflation”.

ONS added that in the financial year to September 2026, borrowing remained below the same period last year, but it was higher than the Office for Budget Responsibility’s forecast.

According to Jasper Kenter, a professorial research fellow in ecological economics at Aberystwyth Business School, for the government to grow the economy without raising inflation levels, there needs to be an understanding of what kind of economy is created.

“The strongest policies improve prosperity, resilience and sustainability at the same time,” Kenter said.

“Growth is less likely to be inflationary when it comes from increasing the economy’s productive capacity rather than simply boosting spending. Measures that improve skills, reduce energy dependence, strengthen local economies and regenerate ecosystems are likely to deliver more lasting benefits than short-term stimulus,” he added.

Moreover, Helen Miller, director of the Institute for Fiscal Studies, said in a media release ahead of the budget that Healey “faces a forecast in which borrowing is still expected to fall in coming years, and the fiscal rules are still being met”.

“Despite that, a ‘steady-as-she-goes’ budget is not an option available to the chancellor. Choosing to stay the course with the inherited tax and spending plans would mean allowing inflation to blow departments’ spending plans off course,” Miller said.

The budget is also expected to reveal new taxes on banks and online marketplaces such as Amazon, Temu and eBay, as well as a funding boost for mayoralties and local authorities.

The biggest four banks collectively made about profits of 15 billion pounds ($19.9bn) in the first six months of this year. Trade unions are calling for higher taxes on those earnings, the BBC has reported.

According to the BBC, the Treasury is leaning towards changing a 2023 surcharge rate on banks, which would raise about 2 billion pounds ($2.6bn).

On marketplaces such as Amazon, Healey is reportedly looking to crack down on foreign sellers who avoid paying VAT – a UK sales tax – which is expected to raise as much as 1 billion pounds ($1.3bn) and help fund business rate cuts for high street shops, The Times reported.

According to The Guardian newspaper, Healey is expected to allocate about 1.42 trillion pounds ($1.8 trillion) this year for day-to-day spending and public investment, with about 100 billion pounds ($132.8bn) going on debt interest.

Kenter, of Aberystwyth Business School, told Al Jazeera that he expects “targeted support rather than large-scale tax cuts or rises” in the budget announcement.

“The government appears keen to signal empathy with the pressures many people are facing. Addressing the harsh cliff edge in carer’s allowance and expanding parental pay are good examples of this,” he said.

Some of the budget’s contents have already been announced, including ending the carers’ allowance limit and removing tariffs on a range of food items, including chocolate and beans, to make them cheaper for shoppers.

Pensioners are also expected to be shielded from income tax through the introduction of a new personal allowance, while Healey is expected to add another 1 billion pounds ($1.3bn) to the 39 billion pounds ($51.8bn) planned for social and affordable housing in England over the next decade.

“Pensioners will benefit from another substantial increase in the state pension, while low-paid workers will benefit from increases in the minimum wage. For most households, the bigger determinants of living standards will remain wages, inflation and energy costs rather than any new tax measures announced in the budget,” Kenter explained.

Last month, Burnham announced a new national care service to provide free personal care for elderly people. As costs of care for the elderly have soared in the UK, this was a major issue from the outset of Burnham’s premiership.

He said the plan would be introduced in phases and would be fully funded from public spending and savings from scrapping the state pension triple lock – an annual increase in state pension that goes up with inflation, wages or a fixed rate of 2.5 percent, whichever is highest.

A report on how this will be implemented is due in summer 2027.

Amid high gas and oil prices as a result of the US-Israeli war with Iran and the subsequent closure of the Strait of Hormuz, energy prices worldwide have increased, with Brent crude futures at $115.90 a barrel on Wednesday.

In the UK, energy prices are predicted to reach nearly 2,000 pounds ($2,655) a year for households in January after energy consultancy Cornwall Insight projected in its latest forecast last month that the government’s cap on energy prices is expected to increase by 16 percent.

On energy bills, reports suggest the chancellor is expected to announce help for households in the budget by scrapping standing charges for energy supply, among other things.

A boy has died and four members of his family are critical after a fire ripped through a Bronx apartment early Wednesday, according to a report.

Some 130 fire and EMS personnel were dispatched to 320 Morris Ave just after 12:50 a.m., responding to a blaze that broke out in an 11th-floor apartment at the Patterson Houses complex, according to the FDNY.

Two adults and three boys were rescued and they are believed to be part of the same family, WABC reported. FDNY did not confirm their relationship.

One boy died after being rushed to Jacobi Hospital in critical condition. Another boy is critical after being rushed to the same hospital.

A boy was rushed to Harlem Hospital in critical condition, while a man, and 33-year-old woman were transported to Lincoln Hospital in critical condition.

A lithium-ion battery was found at the scene but it’s unclear if it caused the blaze.

The fire was under control by 2:05 a.m.

FDNY. به گزارش WABC، دو بزرگسال و سه پسر نجات یافتند و گمان می‌رود که آنها بخشی از یک خانواده باشند. FDNY رابطه آنها را تایید نکرد. یک پسر پس از انتقال سریع به بیمارستان Jacobi در شرایط بحرانی جان باخت. پسر دیگری پس از انتقال سریع به همان بیمارستان وخیم است. پسری در شرایط وخیم به بیمارستان هارلم منتقل شد، در حالی که یک مرد و یک زن 33 ساله در شرایط وخیم به بیمارستان لینکلن منتقل شدند. یک باتری لیتیوم یونی در محل پیدا شد، اما مشخص نیست که آیا باعث آتش سوزی شده است یا خیر. آتش تا ساعت 2:05 بامداد کنترل شد.

news.originalContent:
UN agency expresses ‘grave concern’ in Hebron and warns of echoes of 2025 ‘Iron Wall’ operation.

The Israeli army has continued its incursions into Hebron as its lockdown of the occupied West Bank’s largest city entered its sixth day.

Israeli forces raided several neighbourhoods in Hebron city as well as towns across the wider governorate on Wednesday, tightening restrictions at the entrances to the city, Anadolu news agency reported.

Troops also raided the Fawwar refugee camp south of Hebron about midnight, searching several Palestinian homes.

The Israeli army carried out raids in other areas across the occupied West Bank, detaining four Palestinians in Tulkarem, the Wafa news agency reported.

Those detained included a journalist and his two brothers, alongside an officer working for the Palestinian General Intelligence Service.

In the town of Beita, south of Nablus, troops fired tear gas at protesters demonstrating against the demolition of two homes belonging to the families of two Palestinian prisoners.

A Palestinian man sustained fractures to his hand after Israeli forces beat him during an attack on the village of Yasid, north of Nablus.

In Burin village, troops raided homes and converted several into military barracks, Wafa reported.

Schools in southern Nablus have been ordered to switch to remote learning to protect students and staff.

The raids come a day after the United Nations Relief and Works Agency (UNRWA) expressed “grave concern” over Israel’s continued incursions into Hebron, which have displaced nearly 5,000 Palestinians, warning that “collective punishment” violates international law.

“A near-total lockdown across large parts of Hebron has severely restricted residents’ freedom of movement and their ability to access critical services,” Roland Friedrich, the director of UNRWA Affairs for the occupied West Bank, said in a post on X.

“These developments bring alarming echoes of the massive displacement witnessed in the northern occupied West Bank in early 2025, where more than 34,000 Palestine refugees from Jenin, Tulkarem and Nur Shams camps remain forcibly displaced over a year later.”

Israel’s campaign follows the killing of two Israeli soldiers by Palestinian gunmen at a checkpoint last week. The gunmen were later killed by Israeli forces.

Palestinian officials have accused Netanyahu and his hard-right government of exploiting the operation to secure settler votes before Tuesday’s elections in Israel.
news.content: آژانس سازمان ملل «نگرانی شدید» را در الخلیل ابراز می‌کند و نسبت به تکرار عملیات «دیوار آهنین» در سال 2025 هشدار می‌دهد. ارتش اسرائیل در حالی که قرنطینه بزرگ‌ترین شهر کرانه باختری اشغالی وارد ششمین روز شد، به تهاجمات خود به الخلیل ادامه داد. خبرگزاری آنادولو گزارش داد ورودی های شهر. نیروهای ارتش همچنین حدود نیمه شب به اردوگاه آوارگان فوور در جنوب الخلیل یورش بردند و چندین خانه فلسطینی را مورد بازرسی قرار دادند. خبرگزاری وفا گزارش داد که ارتش اسرائیل به مناطق دیگر در سراسر کرانه باختری اشغالی یورش برد و چهار فلسطینی را در طولکرم بازداشت کرد. افراد بازداشت شده شامل یک روزنامه نگار و دو برادرش بودند که در کنار یک افسر سازمان اطلاعات عمومی کار می کردند. در شهر بیتا، در جنوب نابلس، سربازان به سمت معترضانی که در اعتراض به تخریب دو خانه متعلق به خانواده دو اسیر فلسطینی تظاهرات می کردند، گاز اشک آور پرتاب کردند. یک مرد فلسطینی پس از ضرب و شتم وی به روستای یاسید، در شمال نابلس، دست یک مرد فلسطینی شکسته شد. گزارش شده است. به مدارس جنوب نابلس دستور داده شده که برای محافظت از دانش آموزان و کارکنان، به آموزش از راه دور روی بیاورند. این حملات یک روز پس از آن صورت می گیرد که آژانس امداد و کار سازمان ملل متحد (آنروا) "نگرانی شدید" را در مورد ادامه اسرائیل ابراز کرد.

news.originalContent:
As the Russia-Africa Summit gets under way, students in the capital say education is helping to build ties.

Moscow, Russia – Moscow’s Patrice Lumumba Peoples’ Friendship University – better known as RUDN – offers a view of a relationship often discussed in the language of diplomacy, trade and security.

On the eve of the Russia-Africa Summit, due to begin on Wednesday in the capital Moscow, RUDN’s corridors are crowded with students speaking Russian, English, Arabic and dozens of African languages.

There are national celebrations, cultural showcases, food from across the continent and student clubs that turn the campus into what one graduate calls a “mini-city”.

For Africans who have come to study, work and build careers in Russia, the relationship is not an abstract geopolitical project. It is shaped by friendships, education, professional ambitions and the daily experience of life in Moscow.

Keturah Musonda, a Zambian medical graduate, said she has not regretted coming to Russia.

“I think Moscow is one of the best cities in the world,” she said, praising its transport system, the range of events and the opportunities she found beyond the classroom. Her student years at RUDN were filled with theatre, singing, student unions and medical studies. “My student life was quite colourful,” she said.

But it is Russia’s healthcare system that has left the strongest impression on her. Keturah points to the accessibility of ambulances, the investment in specialised equipment and testing, and the particular attention paid to paediatrics.

“In my country, I have never called an ambulance. No one in my family has ever called an ambulance,” she said.

In Moscow, she was struck by specialised children’s clinics and by a system in which paediatric care is treated as a priority. She hopes African countries can invest more heavily in specialist medicine, rather than relying on overstretched general departments inside large hospitals.

Her own journey was made possible through a Russian government scholarship programme, which allows foreign applicants to apply online, submit documents through Russian cultural centres and national authorities, and compete for university places in Russia.

For Moscow, such programmes are an investment in long-term links. For students like Keturah, they are a route to qualifications and experience they hope to take home.

Chinyama Kazombo, another Zambian medical student, describes Russia as a place where he can realise his potential. Over five years, he has made friends from China, Asia, Russia and across Africa, while participating in student events that introduce Russians to Zambian culture.

Zambia’s independence anniversary, he said, was celebrated in Moscow with dance, exhibitions and national traditions.

The ultimate goal is not simply a Russian diploma.

Zambia needs qualified doctors and other specialists, he said, and the education he receives in Russia could help him serve people back home.

Yet Russia will remain part of his life: “I’ll be working with Russians through my entire life … Russia is already part of who I am.”

For Abobakr Mohamed Abbakar Khussein from Sudan, a lecturer at a Moscow university, relations between Russia and Africa are moving in a pragmatic direction, even if they have not yet reached their full potential.

He sees African governments seeking economic links, security cooperation, energy and agricultural partnerships with countries that respect their sovereignty.

Sudan’s relationship with Russia, he noted, dates back 70 years, beginning shortly after Sudanese independence. He pointed to Russian archaeological work around Sudan’s ancient pyramids, as well as the training of Sudanese specialists in medicine, agriculture, the humanities and linguistics. He also sees potential in mining and nuclear cooperation, including with Rosatom.

But he also highlighted the vulnerability created by the war in Ukraine.

Disruption to Russian and Ukrainian grain and cooking-oil exports threatens food security across Africa, he said. His conclusion is direct: African countries need peace, dependable trade routes and practical partnerships.

Aaron Kasonde, a lecturer and assistant professor at RUDN from Zambia, believes agriculture could become one of the most important areas of Russia-Africa cooperation. Africa has vast arable land and a fast-growing, youthful population – the average age is about 19, he said.

The continent needs fertilisers, irrigation systems, investment and technology, Kasonde added.

Several African states remain net food importers, despite having the land and labour needed to produce more. Russia, one of the world’s major wheat and fertiliser producers, could contribute not only through grain exports but through technologies that help African farmers raise yields and build lasting food security, Kasonde believes.

For Hafi Ahmed from Kenya, the next frontier is broader economic cooperation.

Kenya may be smaller than Russia in territory and population, she said, but it has an educated workforce, skilled doctors and nurses, natural resources and significant growth potential. Cultural exchange also matters. She believes Kenyans and Russians have more in common than many assume – an impression reinforced by her close friendship with a Russian.

What unites these voices is neither blind enthusiasm nor a demand that Africa choose geopolitical sides. They want cooperation to produce measurable benefits: Qualified professionals, modern healthcare, food security, technology, jobs and cultural diversity.

Whether the partner is Russia, China, the United States or Europe, the question for African countries is whether that relationship supports national interests and development. On a campus built around international friendship, that is also the message shaping the future of Russia-Africa ties.

After Sunday’s loss to the Dolphins, it is difficult to see a path for Aaron Glenn to keep his job into 2027. The 28-25 defeat was one of those losses that feels hard to come back from.

Here is what I think Glenn and the Jets need to do for him to get a third season as head coach:

The Jets have had two embarrassing losses this season. The first was to the Bears, who ran 89 plays against the Jets, and then Sunday’s loss to the previously winless Dolphins. The Jets were supposed to be past the embarrassment stage this season. Those losses were a theme of last season, particularly in the final month of the year.

Glenn cannot afford any more of these. That means beating teams such as the Dolphins and the Cardinals and the Chargers. It means this week’s game with the Raiders at least should be a back-and-forth game deep into the fourth quarter. It means they can’t get blown out by teams such as the Chiefs, Bills, Patriots and Vikings.

news.originalContent:
Democrats lead national polls as Trump and Obama campaign in key states six days before the US midterm elections.

US Midterms 2026 Latest: We're not in Kansas anymore

With six days to go before the November 3 midterm elections in the United States, Democrats are leading Republicans in national polls, but several key Senate races seem too close to call.

President Donald Trump has stepped up his campaigning, holding two Republican rallies in Texas on Tuesday before heading to Ohio on Wednesday. Ex-President Barack Obama and former Vice President Kamala Harris are also hitting the campaign trail in Georgia for the Democratic Party.

Here is what the latest polls say, what happened on the campaign trail and what to expect on Wednesday.

With less than a week to go before the midterms, a Reuters/Ipsos poll suggests the Democrats are ahead of the Republicans by nine points.

According to the October 22-26 survey, 47 percent of voters support the Democrats, compared with 36 percent who support the Republicans. When undecided voters’ leanings were taken into account, Democrats lead with 50 percent compared with Republicans’ 41 percent.

Trump’s approval rating improved by a percentage point to 32 percent, with 73 percent of US adults saying the cost of living was going in the wrong direction.

In Texas, where Democrats have not won a Senate election since 1988, James Talarico and Republican Ken Paxton are virtually tied in the polls.

Trump has made several trips to the state ahead of the midterms, but the polls indicate a much tighter race than the president has suggested.

“The good people of Texas have probably never seen so much of President Trump. Four visits in seven weeks, which, to put that into context, is twice as many as we saw at the comparable period leading up to the 2024 election, which perhaps shows just how concerned Republicans are,” Al Jazeera’s Phil Lavelle said, reporting from the Texas coastal city of Corpus Christi.

Lavelle said local analysis suggested more Republicans have voted early than Democrats, but Talarico has also been courting Republicans dissatisfied with Trump.

“That doesn’t mean Republicans are voting for Republican candidates,” Lavelle said.

In Michigan, Democrat Abdul El-Sayed and Republican Mike Rogers are also competing in a closely contested Senate race.

“I was a Republican forever, but I became an independent in the last two elections,” Michael Alexander, a Native American backing El-Sayed, told Al Jazeera.

“I don’t really vote for a party any more. I vote for who I think will do the best job.”

Kansas has not elected a Democrat to the Senate since 1932, but Republican incumbent Roger Marshall now faces a close contest against Democrat Adam Hamilton.

The race has brought Trump and his deputy, JD Vance, to the state.

“There’s a reason why we’re seeing not only US President Donald Trump but also Vice President JD Vance heading to Kansas because it’s actually in play,” Al Jazeera’s Patty Culhane said.

According to The Associated Press news agency, both parties and their allied groups have committed about $71m to campaign advertising in the Kansas race, making it the most expensive Senate contest in the state’s history.

Trump addressed two campaign rallies in Texas on Tuesday in support of Paxton.

In Corpus Christi, Trump pointed to a tanker that he said was carrying one million barrels of Venezuelan oil and called it a win for his administration. He also suggested the idea of making Venezuela the 51st US state. The Trump administration has signed an oil deal with Venezuela’s interim leader, Delcy Rodriguez, after abducting socialist President Nicolas Maduro in a military operation in January.

Trump also announced plans to roll back the Biden-era restrictions on methane emissions from oil and gas production, stating that it would help bring down energy prices.

Fuel prices have become a huge election issue as the US-Israel war on Iran continues. Secretary of State Marco Rubio has also joined Trump for a rare campaign-trail appearance in Texas.

In Alaska, Republican Senator Lisa Murkowski has backed Democrat Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins for governor rather than Bernadette Wilson, the Trump-endorsed candidate.

Trump heads to Ohio on Wednesday for his third rally in the state this month, as Republicans try to defend a Senate seat being challenged by former Democratic Senator Sherrod Brown.

The US president is scheduled to speak in Chillicothe at 23:00 GMT. Republican Senator Jon Husted, who took over Vance’s seat when he became vice president, is facing Brown, who is seeking a return to the Senate after losing his seat in 2024.

The two are in a closely contested race, with more than $400m spent or reserved for campaign advertising as of October 8, according to an Axios report.

Republicans are particularly concerned in Texas, Ohio, Kansas and Iowa, where even a few percentage points for a third party could swing the outcome.

Trump is scheduled to hold rallies in Ohio on Wednesday and Iowa on Sunday.

Vance will be in Kinston, North Carolina, campaigning for Republican Senate candidate Michael Whatley, who is running against former Democratic Governor Roy Cooper. The vice president is expected to speak at 16:30 GMT.

In Georgia, former President Obama will campaign in Atlanta alongside Democratic Senator Jon Ossoff and gubernatorial candidate Keisha Lance Bottoms at 20:00 GMT.

Ossoff is running against Republican Mike Collins, while Bottoms faces Republican Rick Jackson in the governor’s race. Trump won Georgia in the 2024 presidential election.

Former Vice President Harris also begins a three-day visit to Georgia on Wednesday, with early in-person voting due to end on Friday, October 30.

In Wisconsin, Marquette Law School will publish its latest statewide poll at 18:15 GMT.

Wednesday’s poll will also examine voters’ views on inflation, tariffs, the US-Israel war on Iran and Trump’s presidency.

در حالی که شش روز تا انتخابات میان دوره ای 3 نوامبر در ایالات متحده باقی مانده است، دموکرات ها در نظرسنجی های ملی پیشتاز جمهوری خواهان هستند، اما به نظر می رسد که چندین رقابت کلیدی در سنا برای برگزاری انتخابات بسیار نزدیک است. دونالد ترامپ، رئیس جمهور آمریکا، مبارزات انتخاباتی خود را افزایش داده و روز سه شنبه دو گردهمایی جمهوری خواهان در تگزاس برگزار کرد و روز چهارشنبه به اوهایو رفت. باراک اوباما، رئیس‌جمهور سابق و کامالا هریس، معاون رئیس‌جمهور سابق نیز در حال ورود به کمپین انتخاباتی حزب دموکرات در گرجستان هستند. در حالی که کمتر از یک هفته تا انتخابات میان دوره ای باقی مانده است، نظرسنجی رویترز/ایپسوس نشان می دهد که دموکرات ها با 9 امتیاز از جمهوری خواهان جلوتر هستند. بر اساس نظرسنجی 22 تا 26 اکتبر، 47 درصد از رأی دهندگان از دموکرات ها حمایت می کنند، در حالی که 36 درصد از جمهوری خواهان حمایت می کنند. وقتی گرایش های رأی دهندگان بلاتکلیف در نظر گرفته شد، دموکرات ها با 50 درصد در مقایسه با جمهوری خواهان 41 درصد پیشتاز هستند. محبوبیت ترامپ با یک درصد بهبود به 32 درصد رسید و 73 درصد از بزرگسالان آمریکایی گفتند که هزینه زندگی در مسیر اشتباهی قرار دارد. در تگزاس، جایی که دموکرات‌ها از سال 1988 در انتخابات سنا پیروز نشده‌اند، جیمز تالاریکو و کن پکستون جمهوری‌خواه عملاً در نظرسنجی‌ها برابر هستند. ترامپ چندین سفر به این ایالت داشته است.

news.originalContent:
The two Nordic leaders are attempting to influence US-brokered talks in Abu Dhabi to end the war in Ukraine.

The leaders of Norway and Finland have held a rare call with Russian President Vladimir Putin to push for an end to the war in Ukraine, ahead of a planned round of United States-brokered talks in Abu Dhabi next month.

The call on Tuesday marked a break from a longstanding policy among Western European heads of state to avoid direct talks with the Russian leader.

Finnish President Alexander Stubb and Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Stoere spoke with Putin for 90 minutes.

US President Donald Trump told reporters on Tuesday that direct talks between the Russian and Ukrainian presidents would happen “very soon”. But with Trump increasingly siding with Putin over Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, Western leaders have been largely sidelined from US-led negotiations to end the Ukraine war.

Gerhard Mangott, an Austrian political analyst, said European governments had “manoeuvred themselves into a dead end” when it came to finding a solution to the war, and Tuesday’s call was an effort to establish a channel for dialogue.

The Nordic leaders are hoping to influence the diplomatic process, following a policy shift by US President Donald Trump in favour of Russia. US ties with Ukraine have sunk to their lowest point in 18 months since Trump blamed Ukrainian strikes on Russian energy facilities for the rise in the cost of diesel, which has doubled in the US this year.

Trump struck a deal with Putin to release Russian diesel stocks to the US and global markets despite sanctions on Russian oil. He also waived newly approved US sanctions on Russia, causing anger in Europe and within his Republican Party, which had largely supported them.

Ukraine also accused the US of restricting its access to Starshield, the military-grade Starlink satellite system that provides missile guidance intelligence.

Stubb described the discussion with Putin as “frank and substantive”.

“We are neighbouring countries to Russia. The outcome of this war will have a direct impact on our and the broader European security. Ending the war requires direct discussions,” the Finnish president said.

Stoere said he and Stubb had “stressed the importance of de-escalation” to Putin.

In a post on X, Stubb said the call “was a follow-up to the meeting in Oslo on 20 October”, referring to talks between US special envoy Steve Witkoff and Zelenskyy, held amid deteriorating relations between Washington and Kyiv. Stubb said the conversation with Putin was prepared “in consultation with Ukraine and the United States .

Stubb stressed that the joint call was held in individual capacities as leaders of Norway and Finland, not as representatives of Europe.

“We emphasised that our support for Ukraine remains unwavering,” Stubb said.

Stubb said all Western allies were consulted on the initiative, and that Ukraine had sought the opening of a new channel of communication, arguing that Europe could not contribute to peace efforts by giving Russia “the silent treatment”.

Norway’s Prime Minister Stoere added: “Talking to the other side does in no way mean that we take off the pressure. So I believe that that is something Europe also should do with voices that can be understood on that side.”

The conversation with Putin was followed up with a call to Zelenskyy.

The Kremlin’s summary of the conversation suggests the Russian president maintained a hard line.

“It was emphasised that achieving a just and long-term peace is possible only if the legitimate interests of the Russian Federation are fully and unconditionally taken into account,” it said.

The Kremlin also made reference to “the confrontational policies of EU and NATO countries, which are contributing to the prolongation of the hostilities”.

Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said the call was “constructive and substantive” adding that “Putin’s position is well known. It’s consistent, and he has spoken about the need to address the root causes.”

But Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov said the Nordic leaders’ call with Putin offered “nothing new” to end the Ukraine conflict, saying that European countries were simply seeking a role in negotiations.

Meanwhile, responding to proposals for direct talks between Putin and Zelenskyy, Russian presidential aide Yury Ushakov said: “The current leader in Kyiv is not legitimate.”

“If Zelenskyy truly wants to hold direct talks, he should come to Moscow, where all necessary conditions will be provided for him, including security,” Ushakov added.

The Norwegian and Finnish leaders’ call with Putin was greeted with scepticism by some European leaders.

“My impression is that everyone wants peace, except for Putin himself. I have quite low expectations for this type of conversation,” Sweden’s Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson told local media.

He said some European leaders had not been informed.

Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen warned against individual diplomatic approaches to Moscow, saying European countries must maintain a united position. “I think Europe should stick together rather than going solo,” she said.

Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said he told Stubb and Stoere that “absolute caution and vigilance are necessary in such contacts”.

In a post on X, Lithuania’s Foreign Affairs Minister Kestutis Budrys said Europe must be at the table when peace in Ukraine is negotiated, “but not as a collection of fragmented voices”.

“Any contact with Russia must be backed by a united position, real leverage and a list of European demands,” Budrys said.
news.content: این دو رهبر کشورهای اسکاندیناوی در تلاشند تا بر مذاکرات با میانجیگری ایالات متحده در ابوظبی برای پایان دادن به جنگ در اوکراین تأثیر بگذارند. رهبران نروژ و فنلاند یک تماس نادر با ولادیمیر پوتین رئیس جمهور روسیه برای فشار بر پایان جنگ در اوکراین، پیش از دور برنامه ریزی شده مذاکرات با میانجیگری ایالات متحده در ابوظبی در ماه آینده برگزار کردند. این تماس روز سه‌شنبه نشان‌دهنده گسست از سیاست دیرینه سران کشورهای اروپای غربی برای اجتناب از گفت‌وگوهای مستقیم با رهبر روسیه بود. الکساندر استاب، رئیس‌جمهور فنلاند و یوناس گار استور، نخست‌وزیر نروژ به مدت 90 دقیقه با پوتین گفتگو کردند. دونالد ترامپ، رئیس‌جمهور آمریکا روز سه‌شنبه به خبرنگاران گفت که مذاکرات مستقیم بین روسای جمهور روسیه و اوکراین "بسیار زود" انجام خواهد شد. اما با حمایت فزاینده ترامپ از پوتین بر سر ولودیمیر زلنسکی، رئیس‌جمهور اوکراین، رهبران غربی تا حد زیادی از مذاکرات تحت رهبری آمریکا برای پایان دادن به جنگ اوکراین کنار گذاشته شده‌اند. گرهارد منگوت، تحلیلگر سیاسی اتریشی، گفت که دولت‌های اروپایی زمانی که نوبت به یافتن راه‌حلی برای جنگ می‌رسد، «خود را به بن‌بست مانور داده‌اند» و درخواست روز سه‌شنبه برای ایجاد یک کانال برای گفت‌وگو تلاشی برای گفتگو بود. پس از تغییر سیاست دونالد ترامپ، رئیس جمهور آمریکا به نفع روسیه، رهبران شمال اروپا امیدوارند بر روند دیپلماتیک تأثیر بگذارند. از زمانی که ترامپ حملات اوکراین به تاسیسات انرژی روسیه را عامل افزایش قیمت گازوئیل دانست که در سال جاری در آمریکا دو برابر شده است، روابط آمریکا با اوکراین به پایین‌ترین سطح خود در 18 ماه گذشته رسیده است.

news.originalContent:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

When you give birth, you’re told to prepare for afterpains, hormonal swings and sleepless nights.

But there’s one postpartum surprise you may not see coming — bloody discharge that can last for weeks, no matter if you gave birth vaginally or by C-section.

The flow is known as lochia, a mix of blood, tissue and mucus left over from pregnancy. The body cleans and heals the uterus by shedding this fluid, a process that often takes four to six weeks.

After going nine months without menstruating, the amount and duration of lochia can be jarring.

It’s utterly defeating to have to stock up on period supplies so soon after giving birth.

What’s worse, tampons are not recommended for at least six weeks after childbirth because they can trap or introduce bacteria into the healing uterus.

That’s why hospitals routinely provide giant maxi pads and disposable mesh boyshorts to new moms.

As you might imagine, ugly undergarments don’t help postpartum mood and self-image. The good news is that Parasol and Postpartum Panty Party have reimagined recovery underwear.

I recently gave birth to twins and tried out Parasol and Postpartum Panty Party products along with the unglamorous hospital offerings.

Finding the right fit was especially imperative because I had a C-section.

About a third (32.4%) of babies born in the US each year are delivered via C-section, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.

The incision site and the rest of my lower abdomen were very sensitive, and I didn’t want to aggravate those areas with uncomfortable underwear.

I started with the hospital’s enormous wingless pad that could have doubled as a wedding dress train. The pad fit well into the boyshorts.

Though the shorts frayed easily, the best thing about them was their high waist.

They gently held the postpartum belly without feeling too tight or painful.

On Day 3 in the hospital, I switched to a pair of green Postpartum Panty Party panties ($27) made with 95% antibacterial bamboo and 5% spandex.

Just under the waistband, it reads: “Proud to be a Badass Mama.” The underwear has a thick lining to collect lochia.

Unfortunately, they fit too snugly and irritated my C-section scar. One of the nurses recommended setting them aside until I healed more.

Once I got home, I tried Parasol’s postpartum underwear ($38.89 for 32). It’s essentially an adult diaper made with better-for-you materials like sustainably sourced wood pulp.

Instead of trying to fit a pad into your underwear, you slip on the highly absorbent diaper and go.

I like the idea of this underwear — ease and simplicity are key for the early postpartum weeks — but they were cut lower than I preferred.

I’m a much bigger fan of Parasol’s diapers for newborns because of their coverage and softness.

I also tried different versions of the Postpartum Panty Party underwear. The “Proud to be a Badass Mama” black boyshorts ($29) provided good coverage and a thick lining.

I love the “Finally, Wine O’Clock Again” granny panties ($17), “Temporarily Out of Service” hipster panties ($19) and the “Worth Every Stitch” ($19) boyfriend-style panties because of their high waists and snug fit.

They are 95% cotton and 5% spandex. I line-dry them, so they don’t shrink.

I added them to my regular lineup after the end of the lochia phase since they don’t have extra lining to absorb blood.

These cheeky panties are not for the self-conscious. I felt a bit embarrassed wearing the “Temporarily Out of Service” underwear while undergoing a mole check by my dermatologist during maternity leave. Wear with caution!

And for women who give birth vaginally, Postpartum Panty Party sells a perineal wash bottle dubbed a Hoo-Ha Hydrant ($15), the Baby’s Out Water Spout ($15) and VaginaStrong Perineal Cooling Pad Liners ($10).

The liners are designed to reduce swelling and speed healing of the perineum, the area between the vagina and the anus that stretches a lot during vaginal birth. This nether region is prone to tearing.

The peri squeeze bottle, meanwhile, acts like a portable bidet to gently clean and soothe the perineum, and the water spout can target hard-to-reach spots.

For their part, hospitals provide plastic squeeze peri bottles, unsurprisingly without bells and whistles.

Along with the ginormous pads and flimsy underwear, it makes quite the parting gift!
news.content: موارد بیشتری از پوشش ما را در نتایج جستجوی خود مشاهده کنید. وقتی زایمان می کنید، به شما گفته می شود که برای دردهای بعد از زایمان، نوسانات هورمونی و شب های بی خوابی آماده شوید. اما یک غافلگیری بعد از زایمان وجود دارد که ممکن است آن را نبینید - ترشحات خونی که می تواند هفته ها طول بکشد، مهم نیست که زایمان طبیعی داشته باشید یا از طریق سزارین. این جریان به عنوان لوچیا، بافت خون و مخاط باقی مانده از خون شناخته می شود. بدن با ریختن این مایع، رحم را تمیز و التیام می‌بخشد، فرآیندی که اغلب چهار تا شش هفته طول می‌کشد. پس از 9 ماه بدون قاعدگی، میزان و مدت لوکیا می‌تواند سخت باشد. ذخیره کردن مواد پریود خیلی زود پس از زایمان کاملاً شکست‌دهنده است. بدتر از آن، تامپون‌ها حداقل شش هفته پس از زایمان برای او توصیه نمی‌شوند. رحم به همین دلیل است که بیمارستان ها به طور معمول پدهای ماکسی غول پیکر و شورت های مشبک یکبار مصرف را به مادران جدید ارائه می دهند. خبر خوب این است که پارتی پاراسل و پارتی پس از زایمان لباس زیر ریکاوری را دوباره طراحی کرده اند. من اخیراً دوقلو به دنیا آوردم و محصولات پارتی پاراسل و پارتی پس از زایمان را همراه با پیشنهادات بی زرق و برق بیمارستانی امتحان کردم. یافتن تناسب مناسب به ویژه ضروری بود زیرا من سزارین کردم. طبق گفته مرکز کنترل و پیشگیری از بیماری، حدود یک سوم (32.4٪) از نوزادانی که هر ساله در ایالات متحده متولد می شوند از طریق سزارین به دنیا می آیند. محل برش

news.originalSummary:
در حالی که جنگ ایران و تبعات اقتصادی آن  به یکی از موضوعات اصلی در آستانه انتخابات میان‌دوره‌ای آمریکا تبدیل شده، رسانه‌ها به انتشار تحلیل و گزارش و بررسی‌های تازه از این جنگ و آنچه پیش روی واشنگتن است ادامه می‌دهند. نظرسنجی‌ها در آمریکا اقتصاد و جنگ را در کانون توجه رای‌دهندگان نشان می‌دهند و به نظر می‌رسد حتی فضای پر هیجان انتخاباتی نیز از توجه به این موضوع نکاسته‌ است.

روزنامه وال‌استریت ژورنا
news.originalContent:
در حالی که جنگ ایران و تبعات اقتصادی آن  به یکی از موضوعات اصلی در آستانه انتخابات میان‌دوره‌ای آمریکا تبدیل شده، رسانه‌ها به انتشار تحلیل و گزارش و بررسی‌های تازه از این جنگ و آنچه پیش روی واشنگتن است ادامه می‌دهند. نظرسنجی‌ها در آمریکا اقتصاد و جنگ را در کانون توجه رای‌دهندگان نشان می‌دهند و به نظر می‌رسد حتی فضای پر هیجان انتخاباتی نیز از توجه به این موضوع نکاسته‌ است.

روزنامه وال‌استریت ژورنال در گزارشی اختصاصی به نقل از مقام‌های آگاه  گفته است آمریکا از طریق کانال‌های نظامی و دیپلماتیک خود به چند کشور حاشیه خلیج فارس خبر داده که برای دور دیگری از حمله «کوتاه و شدید» علیه ایران، پس از انتخابات میان دوره‌ای آمریکا، آماده باشند.

بر اساس این گزارش، این تحول تازه در کنار تغییرات اخیر در آرایش نظامی آمریکا در منطقه، نشانه‌های رو به افزایشی از آمادگی آمریکا و اسراییل برای حمله‌ای سنگین علیه ایران هستند.

بر این اساس، آمریکا یک سامانه پدافند موشکی پاتریوت را از تگزاس به اسرائیل منتقل خواهد کرد. این کشور همچنین به‌تازگی نیروهای خود را از برخی پایگاه‌های آسیب‌پذیر در منطقه جابه‌جا کرده، بخشی از ذخایر مهماتی خود را بازسازی کرده و یک ناوگروه هواپیمابر دیگر به همراه یک واحد اعزامی تفنگداران دریایی را برای پیوستن به حدود ۲۰ شناور جنگی مستقر در منطقه آماده کرده است.

برخی مقام‌های مطلع از «آماده شدن جنگنده‌های آمریکایی برای حمله» خبر داده‌اند و برخی دیگر تاکید کرده‌اند «رئيس جمهور هنوز تصمیم نهایی خود را نگرفته اما به یک حمله وسیع علیه زیرساخت‌ها و تاسیسات هسته‌ای ایران، بعد از انتخابات میان‌دوره‌ای تمایل دارد.»

با این حال، شماری از کارشناسان  هشدار داده‌اند که بیش از ۲۰ هزار حمله‌ای که آمریکا در ایران انجام داده هنوز رفتار تهران را تغییر نداده، و حملات بیشتر نیز ممکن است انگیزه این کشور را برای توسعه برنامه موشکی و هسته‌ای خود بیشتر کند.

دنی سیترونویچ، مقام اطلاعاتی سابق اسرائيل به این روزنامه گفته است « یکی از بزرگ‌ترین اشتباهات  اسرائیل و ایالات متحده  این تصور است که دور دیگری از حملات علیه ایران، از جمله حمله به زیرساخت‌های حیاتی یا حذف مقام‌های ارشد آن، می‌تواند به نوعی موجب سقوط نظام این کشور شود.»

بهنام طالب‌لو مدیر ارشد برنامه ایران در اندیشکده  «بنیاد دفاع از دموکراسی‌» گفته است اگر تهدید فزاینده‌ای مثل بازسازی توان موشکی ایران وجود دارد رئيس جمهوری آمریکا باید استدلال خود در قبال آن علنی و با جزئیات  برای افکار عمومی روشن کند و گرنه  درشرایط فعلی آمریکا با حفظ تحریم‌ها و محاصره، دست بالا را دارد و  باید به همین مسیر ادامه دهد.»

وال‌استریت ژورنال به ارزیابی‌های اطلاعاتی درباره توان باقی‌مانده ایران هم پرداخته و یادآوری کرده که تهران نیز از طریق کانال‌های علنی و محرمانه هشدار داده هرگونه حمله جدید با پاسخ شدید علیه اهداف اقتصادی و غیرنظامی در سراسر منطقه روبه‌رو خواهد شد؛ تهدیدی که به گفته گزارش در شرایطی مطرح می‌شود که آمریکا و متحدان عربش هنوز درگیر جبران کمبود سامانه‌های پدافندی و موشک‌های رهگیر مصرف‌شده در ماه‌های گذشته هستند.

گزیده‌ای از مهم‌ترین خبرها، گزارش‌های میدانی و گفت‌وگوهای اختصاصی را هر هفته در ایمیل خود دریافت کنید.

دو محقق ارشد موسسه رند در مقاله‌ای در فارین پالیسی موضعی مشابه با نظر کارشناسان طرف گفتگوی وال استریت ژورنال را منتشر کرده‌اند. رند یک سازمان پژوهشی  برجسته در حوزه سیاست‌گذاری آمریکاست که ارتباطات عمیق و دیرینه‌‌ای با نهادهای دفاعی و دولتی این کشور دارد و از صداهای تأثیرگذار در واشنگتن در زمینه مسائل امنیت ملی و سیاست عمومی شناخته می‌شود.

این مقاله در نشریه فارین پالیسی با عنوان «کم‌هزینه‌ترین گزینه بد آمریکا در قبال ایران»  استدلال می‌کند که با وجود هزینه‌های سنگین جنگ، واشنگتن نباید به سمت تشدید درگیری برود ولی رویکردی که شکل عقب‌نشینی داشته باشد نیز به ضرر آمریکا خواهد بود.

نویسندگان این مقاله با بررسی سه گزینه پیش روی دولت ترامپ یعنی تشدید جنگ، خروج از درگیری یا ادامه راهبرد فعلی،  گزینه سوم را واقع‌بینانه‌تر می‌دانند. آنها می‌گویند جنگ ایران تاکنون صدها زخمی، ده‌ها میلیارد دلار هزینه، کاهش ذخایر تسلیحاتی و افزایش قیمت انرژی  برای آمریکا به همراه داشته و هنوز نشانه‌ای از پایان آن دیده نمی‌شود. از نگاه آنها بازگشت به جنگ تمام‌عیار یا اشغال بخشی از خاک ایران هزینه‌های انسانی، نظامی و اقتصادی بیشتری به آمریکا تحمیل می‌کند درحالی‌که حفظ محاصره اقتصادی و ادامه فشارهای مالی بر تهران در کنار پاسخ نظامی محدود به حملات تهران از یک سو و پیگیری مذاکرات برای بازگشایی تنگه هرمز و مهار برنامه هسته‌ای ایران از سوی دیگر کماکان بهترین رویکرد پیش روی کاخ سفید است.

فارین پالیسی همچنین هشدار می‌دهد که خروج یکجانبه آمریکا از جنگ، اگر به معنای پایان محاصره اقتصادی ایران باشد، دست بالا را به ایران خواهد داد چرا که  «رفع محاصره دریایی منابع مالی بیشتری را در اختیار تهران و نیروهای نیابتی آن قرارمی‌دهد و نفوذ منطقه‌ای ایران را تقویت کند».

یکی از یادداشت نویسان شبکه بلومبرگ هم به نقل از مقام‌های ارشد حوزه انرژی جهانی گفته است رهبران حوزه انرژی در جهان به طور فزاینده‌ای خود را برای احتمال ادامه وضعیت فرسایشی «نه جنگ نه صلح» میان ایران و آمریکا آماده می‌کنند.

بلومبرگ می‌نویسد بازار نفت آینده جنگ ایران را بعد از نا‌امیدی از توافق سریع یا رویارویی سنگین و نتیجه‌بخش حالا یک سناریوی سوم را بیش‌از پیش جدی می‌بیند: تثبیت یک بن‌بست فرسایشی میان تهران و واشنگتن. بی‌نتیجه ماندن تلاش‌ها برای رسیدن به توافقی دیپلماتیک و عدم عقب نشینی ایران در برابر فشارهای نظامی و اقتصادی به گفته این یادداشت نویس منجر به آن شده که چهره‌های مطرح در بازار نفت، دست کم فعلا درپس پرده خود را برای این سناریوی سوم آماده کنند.

منبع تصویر، US NAVY via Getty Images

با گزارش تازه سنتکام، فرماندهی مرکزی ایالات متحده به کنگره درباره هزینه‌های جنگ، رسانه‌های آمریکا خبر داده‌اند که صورتحساب جنگ با ایران تا نیمه ماه اکتبر از ۴۷ میلیارد دلار گذشته است. براساس گزارش سی‌بی‌اس و نیویورک تایمز بیش از ۶۰ درصد این مبلغ صرف عملیات بمب‌ها، موشک‌ها و سایر مهمات شده است. نیویورک تایمز نوشته است با وجود اینکه در شش هفته گذشته عملیات نظامی مجددی علیه ایران انجام نشده در همین بازه زمانی پنتاگون ۳ و نیم میلیارد دلار هزینه اضافه متحمل شده است.

فهرست هزینه‌های تازه جنگ که به دست کنگره و رسانه‌های آمریکا رسیده جزئيات غیرمحرمانه‌ای است که سنتکام گزارش کرده اما  هزینه تعمیر یا جایگزینی تأسیسات نظامی آمریکا را که در حملات ایران آسیب دیده شامل نمی‌شود.

بر این اساس از  آغاز جنگ ایران در ۲۸ فوریه، ارتش آمریکا معادل ۲۹ میلیارد دلار مهمات مصرف کرده، ۶/۱ میلیارد دلار برای جایگزینی ده‌ها هواپیمای رزمی آسیب‌دیده یا منهدم‌شده و سایر تسلیحات و تجهیزات هزینه کرده و در عین حال بیش از نیم میلیارد دلار صرف جابه‌جایی و پشتیبانی از چند هزار نیروی ویژه مستقر در منطقه کرده است.

هزینه استقرار بیش از ده‌ها ناو جنگی، از جمله چندین ناو هواپیمابر، ۱/۵ میلیارد دلار بوده و حفظ و پشتیبانی نیروهای ارتش آمریکا در منطقه  نیز۲.۱ میلیارد دلار هزینه داشته است.

یکی از مقام‌های کنگره به روزنامه نیویورک تایمز گفته است  ارتش آمریکا بیش از۲۴ میلیون دلار برای «خدمات پزشکی داخلی» به نیروهای نظامی آمریکایی هزینه کرده است. بر اساس آمار پنتاگون دست کم ۸۰۰ سرباز آمریکایی در این جنگ زخمی شده‌اند.

مقام‌های کنگره به رسانه‌های آمریکا گفته‌اند که ارقام اعلام‌شده احتمالاً کمتر از هزینه واقعی جنگ هستند و مثلا  شامل ۱/۵ میلیارد دلار هزینه سوخت و سایر مخارجی  که دولت ترامپ برای آن بودجه تکمیلی درخواست کرده نمی‌شود. پنتاگون از کنگره  ۷۰ میلیارد دلار بودجه اضطراری نظامی درخواست کرده تا هزینه‌های جنگ ایران را پوشش دهد.
news.content:
در حالی که جنگ ایران و تبعات اقتصادی آن  به یکی از موضوعات اصلی در آستانه انتخابات میان‌دوره‌ای آمریکا تبدیل شده، رسانه‌ها به انتشار تحلیل و گزارش و بررسی‌های تازه از این جنگ و آنچه پیش روی واشنگتن است ادامه می‌دهند. نظرسنجی‌ها در آمریکا اقتصاد و جنگ را در کانون توجه رای‌دهندگان نشان می‌دهند و به نظر می‌رسد حتی فضای پر هیجان انتخاباتی نیز از توجه به این موضوع نکاسته‌ است.

روزنامه وال‌استریت ژورنال در گزارشی اختصاصی به نقل از مقام‌های آگاه  گفته است آمریکا از طریق کانال‌های نظامی و دیپلماتیک خود به چند کشور حاشیه خلیج فارس خبر داده که برای دور دیگری از حمله «کوتاه و شدید» علیه ایران، پس از انتخابات میان دوره‌ای آمریکا، آماده باشند.

بر اساس این گزارش، این تحول تازه در کنار تغییرات اخیر در آرایش نظامی آمریکا در منطقه، نشانه‌های رو به افزایشی از آمادگی آمریکا و اسراییل برای حمله‌ای سنگین علیه ایران هستند.

بر این اساس، آمریکا یک سامانه پدافند موشکی پاتریوت را از تگزاس به اسرائیل منتقل خواهد کرد. این کشور همچنین به‌تازگی نیروهای خود را از برخی پایگاه‌های آسیب‌پذیر در منطقه جابه‌جا کرده، بخشی از ذخایر مهماتی خود را بازسازی کرده و یک ناوگروه هواپیمابر دیگر به همراه یک واحد اعزامی تفنگداران دریایی را برای پیوستن به حدود ۲۰ شناور جنگی مستقر در منطقه آماده کرده است.

برخی مقام‌های مطلع از «آماده شدن جنگنده‌های آمریکایی برای حمله» خبر داده‌اند و برخی دیگر تاکید کرده‌اند «رئيس جمهور هنوز تصمیم نهایی خود را نگرفته اما به یک حمله وسیع علیه زیرساخت‌ها و تاسیسات هسته‌ای ایران، بعد از انتخابات میان‌دوره‌ای تمایل دارد.»

با این حال، شماری از کارشناسان  هشدار داده‌اند که بیش از ۲۰ هزار حمله‌ای که آمریکا در ایران انجام داده هنوز رفتار تهران را تغییر نداده، و حملات بیشتر نیز ممکن است انگیزه این کشور را برای توسعه برنامه موشکی و هسته‌ای خود بیشتر کند.

دنی سیترونویچ، مقام اطلاعاتی سابق اسرائيل به این روزنامه گفته است « یکی از بزرگ‌ترین اشتباهات  اسرائیل و ایالات متحده  این تصور است که دور دیگری از حملات علیه ایران، از جمله حمله به زیرساخت‌های حیاتی یا حذف مقام‌های ارشد آن، می‌تواند به نوعی موجب سقوط نظام این کشور شود.»

بهنام طالب‌لو مدیر ارشد برنامه ایران در اندیشکده  «بنیاد دفاع از دموکراسی‌» گفته است اگر تهدید فزاینده‌ای مثل بازسازی توان موشکی ایران وجود دارد رئيس جمهوری آمریکا باید استدلال خود در قبال آن علنی و با جزئیات  برای افکار عمومی روشن کند و گرنه  درشرایط فعلی آمریکا با حفظ تحریم‌ها و محاصره، دست بالا را دارد و  باید به همین مسیر ادامه دهد.»

وال‌استریت ژورنال به ارزیابی‌های اطلاعاتی درباره توان باقی‌مانده ایران هم پرداخته و یادآوری کرده که تهران نیز از طریق کانال‌های علنی و محرمانه هشدار داده هرگونه حمله جدید با پاسخ شدید علیه اهداف اقتصادی و غیرنظامی در سراسر منطقه روبه‌رو خواهد شد؛ تهدیدی که به گفته گزارش در شرایطی مطرح می‌شود که آمریکا و متحدان عربش هنوز درگیر جبران کمبود سامانه‌های پدافندی و موشک‌های رهگیر مصرف‌شده در ماه‌های گذشته هستند.

گزیده‌ای از مهم‌ترین خبرها، گزارش‌های میدانی و گفت‌وگوهای اختصاصی را هر هفته در ایمیل خود دریافت کنید.

دو محقق ارشد موسسه رند در مقاله‌ای در فارین پالیسی موضعی مشابه با نظر کارشناسان طرف گفتگوی وال استریت ژورنال را منتشر کرده‌اند. رند یک سازمان پژوهشی  برجسته در حوزه سیاست‌گذاری آمریکاست که ارتباطات عمیق و دیرینه‌‌ای با نهادهای دفاعی و دولتی این کشور دارد و از صداهای تأثیرگذار در واشنگتن در زمینه مسائل امنیت ملی و سیاست عمومی شناخته می‌شود.

این مقاله در نشریه فارین پالیسی با عنوان «کم‌هزینه‌ترین گزینه بد آمریکا در قبال ایران»  استدلال می‌کند که با وجود هزینه‌های سنگین جنگ، واشنگتن نباید به سمت تشدید درگیری برود ولی رویکردی که شکل عقب‌نشینی داشته باشد نیز به ضرر آمریکا خواهد بود.

نویسندگان این مقاله با بررسی سه گزینه پیش روی دولت ترامپ یعنی تشدید جنگ، خروج از درگیری یا ادامه راهبرد فعلی،  گزینه سوم را واقع‌بینانه‌تر می‌دانند. آنها می‌گویند جنگ ایران تاکنون صدها زخمی، ده‌ها میلیارد دلار هزینه، کاهش ذخایر تسلیحاتی و افزایش قیمت انرژی  برای آمریکا به همراه داشته و هنوز نشانه‌ای از پایان آن دیده نمی‌شود. از نگاه آنها بازگشت به جنگ تمام‌عیار یا اشغال بخشی از خاک ایران هزینه‌های انسانی، نظامی و اقتصادی بیشتری به آمریکا تحمیل می‌کند درحالی‌که حفظ محاصره اقتصادی و ادامه فشارهای مالی بر تهران در کنار پاسخ نظامی محدود به حملات تهران از یک سو و پیگیری مذاکرات برای بازگشایی تنگه هرمز و مهار برنامه هسته‌ای ایران از سوی دیگر کماکان بهترین رویکرد پیش روی کاخ سفید است.

فارین پالیسی همچنین هشدار می‌دهد که خروج یکجانبه آمریکا از جنگ، اگر به معنای پایان محاصره اقتصادی ایران باشد، دست بالا را به ایران خواهد داد چرا که  «رفع محاصره دریایی منابع مالی بیشتری را در اختیار تهران و نیروهای نیابتی آن قرارمی‌دهد و نفوذ منطقه‌ای ایران را تقویت کند».

یکی از یادداشت نویسان شبکه بلومبرگ هم به نقل از مقام‌های ارشد حوزه انرژی جهانی گفته است رهبران حوزه انرژی در جهان به طور فزاینده‌ای خود را برای احتمال ادامه وضعیت فرسایشی «نه جنگ نه صلح» میان ایران و آمریکا آماده می‌کنند.
